Let <MATH_0001> be a Noetherian scheme. Let <MATH_0002> be a subset closed
under specialization.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> Let <MATH_0003> be a torsion abelian sheaf on <MATH_0004>
whose support is contained in <MATH_0005>. Then <MATH_0006>
is a filtered colimit of constructible abelian sheaves <MATH_0007>
such that for each <MATH_0008> the support of <MATH_0009> is contained in
a closed subset contained in <MATH_0010>.
<STRUCT_0003> Let <MATH_0011> be a Noetherian ring and <MATH_0012> a sheaf
of <MATH_0013>-modules on <MATH_0014> whose support is contained in <MATH_0015>.
Then <MATH_0016>
is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves of
<MATH_0017>-modules <MATH_0018> such that for each <MATH_0019>
the support of <MATH_0020> is contained in a closed subset
contained in <MATH_0021>.
<STRUCT_0004>

Proof of (1). We can write <MATH_0001>
with <MATH_0002> constructible abelian by
Lemma <REF_0001>.
By Proposition <REF_0002>
the image <MATH_0003>
of the map <MATH_0004> is constructible.
Thus <MATH_0005> and the support
of <MATH_0006> is contained in <MATH_0007>.
Since the support of <MATH_0008> is constructible
(by our definition of constructible sheaves), we see
that its closure is also contained in <MATH_0009>, see for example
Topology, Lemma
<REF_0003>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
The proof in case (2) is exactly the same and we omit it.
